component: P16 independent externally pinned policy validation
constraints: Immutable UTF-8 JSON at most 65536 bytes and depth eight; closed metadata, bounded keys/revocations and exact-byte SHA-256.
Caller supplies authenticated pin, trusted time and revision/time floors. No enrollment, disk, network, implicit clock or persistent state.
No specified hardware, embedded OS, throughput, hard deadline or process-memory budget.
alternatives: CPython lexical hooks plus native hashlib SHA-256.
CUE declarative constraints with an exact-byte/context wrapper.
Java/Kotlin Jackson token streaming and provider SHA-256.
Rust Serde custom lexical admission and sha2.
Erlang/Elixir binary data, JSON callbacks and crypto hashing.
rationale: KEEP the explicit lexical hooks and native hash boundary: the same validated bytes are hashed, all key metadata is checked, and invalid scalar/lexical inputs retain closed rejection behavior.

Value/schema validation alone does not replace exact raw-byte pins or authenticate the pin provider. CUE is credible for configuration tooling but would still need those boundaries. Native/managed token parsers remain credible alternatives.

Eight focused policy methods pass; disabling the raw-byte pin comparison causes an expected assertion failure. This supplies contract and negative-control evidence, not full alternative implementation parity.
No requirement or measurement establishes a material alternative advantage. Existing language, installed tools, familiarity and rewrite cost are not retention criteria.
limits: Caller-supplied pins and floors can be rolled back; this API has no persistence or same-revision equivocation detection.
A valid policy may revoke every signer. Successful policy validation is not a successful passport or evidence qualification.
Candidate comparison is source-based; no CUE/JVM/Rust/BEAM implementation was benchmarked.
No comparative performance ranking, whole-lane completion, MLS/CNSA qualification, availability or physical timing claim.
No migration winner is established under the specified bounded offline constraints; no winning migration is deferred.
